content.comment_body: Good afternoon, everyone. I am seeking help again. I am trying to connect the following devices: 1. PC 2. [company_name] PLC [product_name] 3. HMI [product_name] (connected via Ethernet) My goal is to press a button on the HMI and have the output (Q1) on the [product_name] become active, but so far I have not been able to accomplish this. I have attached a picture of my project.

Physical inputs (I) on the [product_name] can only be activated by hardware signals. Input I1 cannot be set by the HMI. To achieve this, the HMI should set a bit in the VM area of the [product_name], which you then use in the [product_name] program logic as a network input.
The attachment includes a section from a [product_name] user guide. This might be helpful for you.
Thank you everyone. The solution worked successfully.

analysis.insight_summary: Users struggled with integrating a third-party HMI and a [company_name] PLC [product_name], particularly regarding how to trigger outputs remotely. The main challenge was a misunderstanding about the difference between physical and virtual inputs on the [product_name]. The community clarified that the HMI should interact via the VM area for virtual input operation, which solved the user's issue and made the desired automation possible.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants direct control of the [product_name] output Q1 via the HMI button without changing any physical wiring. They expect immediate and reliable feedback when operating from the HMI.
pain_keywords: lack of clear documentation for HMI-PLC setup
